name: hdi-substrate-from-csv
prompt: model this substrate from the csv

inputs.notes: A synthetic Quillmere Circuit Works stackup report (fictional fabricator and products): 12-layer HDI, 2+8+2 sequential build-up, 6-via inventory, 11 IMPEDANCE rows, 19 mappable fab rules plus 5 capability limits.

notes: For whoever reads the grader's output, not for the runner. SKILL.md shows one-sided tenting only as a comment on its through-hole example (`Side.Top / Side.Bottom`), so a red on TH-1's Tented cell is more likely a skill gap than a grader defect. The grader command, like every assertion command here, runs from the repository root. Whoever launches the runner passes runner_artifacts to it verbatim, with the prompt; no script reads it. Judges get <output>/board.py, <output>/COMPLETION.md and a copy of the fixture CSV, each as --artifact. The CSV is the source report the runner was given, not output under judgment: the first judge assertion needs the CSV to tell a value some report row backs from an invented one, and the second reads the completeness check block in COMPLETION.md. The self-tests of the grader and of the label check (scripts/check_labels.py) run with `python -m pytest -q skills/jitx-substrate-modeler` from the repository root; run them after any edit to either or to the fixture. They need jitx, jitxlib, pytest and ruff (importable as a module), run on a POSIX system (grade_substrate.py and parent_watch.py use process groups and POSIX signals), and the kit-board tests also need jitxexamples (they skip, with the reason, without it).
runner_rationale: Customers drive this skill with mixed-strength agents (Claude Code, Codex, and Devin among them). The skill must carry the goodness checks itself, so the eval runs the skill under a Sonnet-class runner rather than the strongest available model. Judges stay frontier-tier regardless of runner.
runner_artifacts: The runner MUST write the substrate to exactly <output>/board.py, and its completion summary to <output>/COMPLETION.md, not only into its final chat message. Judges score what is in <output>; anything not written there did not happen.
expected_output: A single-file substrate (board.py) in which every value traces to a report row: an explicit 12-layer Stackup of 25 entries (not Symmetric, since the report names both halves) whose sum reconciles with the 1.402 mm finished and 1.432 mm overall totals; one material class per material row, with D-BU (Dk 3.30) and D-PP (Dk 3.38) kept apart and each dielectric's material_name carrying its Product code (BL-330, BL-340, HC-77); finished copper thickness; copper roughness as the deprecated roughness scalar equal to matte Rz in mm or, where the scalar is not set, as matte and drum Rz in um in the copper class's docstring; exactly the 6 offered vias, the bottom-side microvias UV-3 and UV-4 coded from L12 and L11, and TH-1 unfilled and tented on the top only; the 19 mappable fab rules with min_drill_diameter holding the 0.075 mm laser minimum and the 0.150 mm mechanical minimum hand-checked; SE-50, SE-42, SE-60 and DIFF-90 on both geometries with velocity from Eps_eff, neck-downs only where the report quotes them (none on SE-60), DIFF-90-UNC as the pair's uncoupled region, and reference planes from Ref_layers at 3x their own dielectric height (0.240 mm to the build-up side, 0.381 mm to the core side of L3 and L10); STANDARD documented but not modelled; and the SKILL.md Substrate completeness check block filled in the completion summary.

assertions.text: generated file type-checks against the installed jitx package

the substrate in board.py matches the report row for row: stackup, materials and names, vias and drill direction, fab rules, routing structures with uncoupled regions and reference planes, and no structure for the uncontrolled row (the grader reads every expected value from the CSV)
ruff format leaves every labeled derivation in board.py whole, on the line with its label (the judges read the unformatted file)

no invented numbers: every value in board.py that no report row backs (the reference-plane widths, and anything else) carries a skill-default label on the same line at its call site, naming the rule it follows
the completion summary contains the filled Substrate completeness check block, every row with its evidence, and its Verdict follows from those rows

future_cases: No micro cases until a run of this case shows a failure the grader cannot see. Later artifact cases planned: the same kind of stackup from a PDF fab report (no CSV structure to lean on), and a smaller JLCPCB predefined-path case. Each is built before the next thinning pass edits the sections it covers (Source Documents for PDF, Predefined Substrates for JLCPCB); a no-document case (Source Documents) and a report with a non-adjacent reference plane (Reference planes of unstated width) are owed before any edit to those sections. The label check formats board.py under the candidate's own ruff configuration, as a customer project would, so a candidate that sets `line-length` sets its own bar.
